sections.text: I am the Wind among purifiers, the King Rama among warriors; I am the Crocodile among the fishes, and I am the Ganges among rivers.
I am the Beginning, the Middle and the End in creation; among sciences, I am the science of Spirituality; I am the Discussion among disputants.
Of letters I am A; I am the copulative in compound words; I am Time inexhaustible; and I am the all-pervading Preserver.

We have been discussing Chapter 10, Vibhuti yoga, Yoga of Divine Glories. As we have seen, Arjuna, after listening to the whole discourse from Bhagavan on the nature of the Supreme self, said, But I need to know more. So in verse 18 he says: Vistarena Atmano Yogam Vibhutim cha Janardana, Bhuyah Kathaya Triptir hi Shrinvato Nasti Me Amritam. Tell me again in detail, O Janardana, your Yoga power and your immanent glory, because I do not feel satisfied hearing your life-giving, nectar-like speech. In other words, he said, give me some examples. So Bhagavan said: Divya hi Atma Vibhutayah , my glories are divine.
Pradhanyataha Kuru Shreshtha Na Astyantah Vistarasya Me. There is no end to this glory, but I can give you some prominent examples. So Bhagavan clearly clarified to Arjuna: Im going to give you some prominent examples.
They do not constitute my entire glory, but they will give you some idea of where to see my presence. So we have been seeing many examples, right from the Vedic period to the Puranic period. And Bhagavan is now even coming down to our day-to-day experiences.
Pavanaha Pavatamasmi , something which we experience in phenomenal nature. Everything and every being is nothing but my own self, because he said everything proceeds from me and I am the source of all things and beings. There is no other thing which has created this universe.
When we see an effect, there have to be two causes. One is the efficient cause , somebody who knows how to make that thing come into existence. And one is the material to create that thing.
Take pizza: we need a pizza maker and pizza ingredients. So if you see pizza here, you cant simply say, Well, the pizza just appeared here. We are Chinmaya Mission, we are divine people.
We dont need to order pizza. Pizza just appears here. We know that an intelligent person will not believe that. He knows that if there is pizza there, there is a pizza maker and he had the ingredients for the pizza.
So the same way, if this world exists, there is the material cause and efficient cause. Material cause is something which we have difficulty understanding. We think if Bhagavan knows everything, obviously he knows how to create this world.
The problem is where did he find the material? How do we create something? Im an architect, so I can create buildings. Because I know how to design building. Just knowing how to create building doesnt create building.
I need to have materials. Go to Home Depot or Lowes to buy that material. Ask Home Depot, Where do you get materials? We get them from our suppliers. So you can go up to the source of the material, where it came from.
In this case, if we find the source of the material which Bhagavan used to create this Jagat, you can always say that Bhagavan found the material from X. Then X becomes greater than the Bhagawan who created it. Go to X and say, Where did you get the material? From Y. Then Y becomes greater than X because he had the original material.
Ask Y, Where did you get the material? Z had the material, and then Z becomes greater than Y. So this exercise is futile because we cannot get to the ultimate source of the material. You have to come to the conclusion that Bhagavan himself was the source of the material.
In Bhagawan, theres only one thing which he did not have to buy, borrow, or steal , that is his own self. Everything we acquire in this world, we bought from somebody, borrowed from somebody, or took from somebody. But one thing I never had to acquire is my own self.
That which I call I. I did not acquire it from anywhere. I didnt buy from anywhere. So thats the only material available to Bhagavan.
So he created this Jagat using his knowledge of creating this universe as an efficient cause. And he also used the material available to him with his own self. So he became the material cause and the efficient cause for this universe.
Therefore he said, everything proceeds from me and I am the source of all things. However, that is not something for us to easily understand. So give me some examples of glories.
It may be difficult to find glory in something which is average. But we can find it in something which is really excellent. If you have a water jug and you put just a little salt in it, and you taste it, you wont know that there is salt in it.
But if theres a lot of salt in it and you taste it, you know theres salt in it. The Bhagawan has been giving several prominent examples. Sarjanam, Adihicha, Antacha, Madhyamcha Evam, Aham, Arjunah.
In the creation for anything which is created and the beginning, the middle and the end, there is no other material to create anything, to sustain anything or destroy anything. The same material which was used to create this Jagat, everything in Jagat in this universe is also created by the same original material. So Bhagawan said, any creation you see in this world, I am the beginning, the middle and the end.
In verse 33 he says, Aksaranam Akaro Asmi. In the previous verse he said, among all the sounds, I am the one syllable, Om. Because Om is the primordial sound.
That is the sound which is the most basic sound out of which all the other variation of sounds come into existence. As I said, its like three color printing. There are only three cartridges in your printer.
But when you print a picture, permutation combination of those three colors created this wonderful picture which is a variety of colors. So A-U-M is like the source of all the sounds. Om is the sum total of all the sounds that we hear in this world.
Out of Om, the first sound is A. A signifies creation, U signifies sustenance, and M signifies dissolution. So when you close your mouth, its Ma.
I heard Anup Jilotra telling a joke. He was teaching a female student. He said she would do Sa-Re-Ga-Ma, but when it comes to Ma, she would skip it.
He said, Why are you skipping Ma? She said, Ma, I have to close my mouth so my lipstick gets spoiled. So Ma , you are closing your lips, signifying the dissolution. A comes from your belly, signifying creation. Aksaranam Akaro Asmi.
Among the letters, I am A. In every language, the alphabet starts with A, and without a vowel you cannot make any word. And in Sanskrit there is a preponderance of the A sound.
Therefore it is such a sweet-sounding language. Among the compound words in Sanskrit, I am Dvandva. Those of us who have learned a little bit of Sanskrit know there are several types of compound words.
I know only one very well: Bahuvrihi Samasa. Yasya Kantah Nilah , whose neck is blue? Neela Kantha. Thats a Bahuvrihi Samasa.
So two words, Neela and Kantha, when you combine them become Neelakantha. Thats what I remember from my 8th standard Sanskrit. In this, Neela is actually almost like an adjective.
It does not have the same value as Kantha. Neela is just the attribute of that Kantha. But in Dvandva Samasa, when two words are used, they both retain their own identity.
Sita-Ram , Sita and Ram both maintain their own identity, their own importance. Therefore Dvandva is considered the most prominent Samasa. Bhagavan says among the compound words, I am Dvandva , that which retains the value of both.
Some commentators have commented that it also may be indicating the Self and non-Self. So this entire world of ours is made up of something which we call the Self , that is me , and something which is not me, which is the non-Self. In Vedanta, this body, mind, and intellect are non-Self.
They are not really permanent. I am permanent , the I feeling is permanent. This beautiful combination of Self and non-Self which we see in our Jagat , the Self remains the Self, and still the non-Self retains its own identity as a plurality in this world. So therefore Bhagawan says: among compound words, I am Dvandva.
Aham Eva Akshayaha Kalaha. I am that ever-existing time. He said among the reckoners, among the measures, I am time.
Everything we know is defined in space and time. Indian philosophers have given more importance to time. They say time is fundamental, and space is an emergent quality of time.
So Bhagawan said, I am time. Among all the ways we measure things, I am time. In all measurement, time is the most important one.
He said I am that infinite time. It seems like to us that it is flowing and going. But time remains constant.
Its our experiences that change. Our experience of time starts with one event followed by a second event. If theres only one event, there is no time.
When only the first event occurs, there is no time. We measure time between two events. Therefore, the measure of time in English is called second, not first. There is no first in time , only seconds.
So here he says I am that infinite time, not the finite time perceived through your senses. Dhata Aham Vishwato Mukaha , and I am also the Karma Phaladata. I am also the supporter, the dispenser of all your experiences.
I experience as long as Im alive, as long as Im conscious. So my consciousness is the dispenser of all my thoughts and experiences. Dhata Vishwato Mukaha , facing everywhere, that Self which is in me.
Facing everywhere and getting experience of everything is the same self in you. That Self is facing everywhere, gaining all the experience outside. So when you put it together, Bhagavan is everywhere.
No matter where you see, he is there. The next verse says Mrityuh Sarva Harascha , I am death among all that takes things away from you. You can lose things in an accident.
You can lose things in various ways in life. We lose money in the stock market. But you see, youre still left with something.
I may lose money, but Ill have my health. I may be out of health, but Im still alive. So theres something left.
I lost something, but when I die, I lose everything. Theres nothing left for me. Therefore, I am death , it takes away everything from you.
You cannot take anything with you. Therefore its Mrityu Sarva Haraschaham , the greatest taker, who takes everything that you think is yours. Udbhavascha Bhavisyatam.
The translation in the book is slightly confusing. It says, I am the prosperity of those who are to be prosperous. s not really the appropriate interpretation of Udbhava. Udbhava means to come into existence. I am the source of all that is coming to be in the future. Not only am I the source of all things and beings in the present that you see, but I am also the source of everything that will come into existence in the future.
In other words, past, present, and future are just concepts of my mind. There is only one existence, and it exists all the time. And therefore anything which is created in that existence is nothing but the expression of the same supreme reality which is all-pervading, everlasting, omnipresent, omniscient.
Kirtihi Shri Vakcha Narinam Smriti Medha Dhriti Kshamah. All women can take some pride here. All the good qualities listed are feminine.
Bhagawan says I am these feminine qualities. Fame, prosperity, speech, memory, intelligence, firmness and forgiveness. All these qualities are manifest in people because of my presence.

These verses reveal the divine in language, knowledge, and time itself. Among letters, Krishna is A (Akara) - the first sound, present in every vowel, essential for all speech. Among compound words, He is Dvandva - the type that preserves the equal identity of both components (like Sita-Ram where neither subsumes the other). This points to the coexistence of Self and non-self, spirit and matter, maintaining their distinct identities while unified. Among sciences, He is Adhyatma-vidya - the science of the Self, supreme among all knowledge because it reveals the knower behind all knowing.
Most profound is Aham eva akshayah kalah - I am inexhaustible Time. Time seems to devour everything, yet Krishna identifies with that which makes all experience possible. Without time, there is no before and after, no change, no experience. The measure of time in English is second (not first) because time only appears when there is a second event to mark against the first. This infinite, unchanging Time is not what we measure with clocks but the eternal present in which all moments arise.
Today, practice awareness of these subtle divine presences. When you speak or write, recognize that the vowel A underlies your words - language itself carries divine essence. When you learn anything, ask: does this knowledge reveal or obscure the knower? The science of Self (Adhyatma-vidya) is supreme because all other knowledge is useless if we do not know who is knowing. Most importantly, notice Time - not as minutes passing but as the unchanging awareness in which all events occur. Can you touch that inexhaustible Time behind your moment-to-moment experience?
